guide_enrichment.narrative:
We are not treating Kansas’ 51-6 opener as proof that the same level of separation carries forward. The Jayhawks produced 613 yards and allowed only 146, but that result is still one game. For us, the more relevant uncertainty is how quickly a reshaped roster settles in: Kansas entered the season with eight returning starters and added 32 transfers.

Our numbers show a plausible path for Middle Tennessee through the passing game and its ability to create scoring opportunities, particularly against areas where Kansas grades less favorably over the longer run. Kansas still showed meaningful upside in the opener, with Isaiah Marshall completing 14 of 19 passes for 246 yards and an offensive line that allowed no sacks. That combination leaves credible cases on both sides, and our overall expectation is essentially aligned with what the market is already asking us to pay. We do not see enough separation to justify a wager.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We are watching Middle Tennessee’s passing offense against Kansas’ pass defense. The question is whether Middle Tennessee can exploit the softer grades in our numbers before Kansas’ pressure disrupts the plan. Leroy Harris III recorded four tackles for loss in the opener, while returning cornerbacks Jalen Todd and Austin Alexander combined for 22 starts last season. If Kansas can generate pressure without compromising that experienced coverage, Middle Tennessee’s clearest route to staying competitive becomes much narrower.

recent_game.fact: Kansas opened the 2026 season with a 51-6 home win over Long Island on Sept. 4.
Kansas produced 613 total yards on 76 plays against Long Island, including 277 rushing yards and 336 passing yards.
Kansas held Long Island to 146 total yards and 35 rushing yards on 33 attempts.
Kansas recorded 11 tackles for loss and did not allow an offensive touchdown against Long Island.

quarterback.fact: Head coach Lance Leipold named redshirt sophomore Isaiah Marshall Kansas' starting quarterback before the 2026 season.
Marshall completed 14 of 19 passes for 246 yards and two touchdowns and rushed seven times for 49 yards against Long Island.
Redshirt junior Cole Ballard is listed as the second quarterback on the Game 2 depth chart; he had completed 35 of 64 career passes for 445 yards and three touchdowns entering the game.

Chase Jenkins transferred to Kansas after starting all 12 regular-season games at quarterback for Rice in 2025, when he passed for 1,025 yards and nine touchdowns and rushed for 531 yards and five touchdowns.

offensive_personnel.fact: Kansas returned three offensive starters from 2025: tight end Carson Bruhn, guard Amir Herring and tackle Calvin Clements.

The Game 2 starting offensive line was listed as Calvin Clements at left tackle, Amir Herring at left guard, Kasen Carpenter at center, Tavake Tuikolovatu at right guard and Nick Morrow at right tackle.
Kansas' offensive line allowed no sacks and only one tackle for loss against Long Island.
Kansas added transfer running backs Yasin Willis from Syracuse, Dylan Edwards from Kansas State and Jalen Dupree from Colorado State for 2026.
Willis rushed 11 times for 72 yards and two touchdowns, Dupree rushed nine times for 35 yards and a touchdown, and Edwards rushed six times for 32 yards against Long Island.
Buffalo transfer Nik McMillan caught six passes for 130 yards and one touchdown in his Kansas debut, extending his streak of 100-yard receiving games to seven.
Wide receiver Nahzae Cox transferred to Kansas from Middle Tennessee and recorded a 47-yard reception in his Kansas debut against Long Island.

defensive_personnel.fact: Kansas returned five defensive starters from 2025: linebacker Trey Lathan, cornerbacks Austin Alexander and Jalen Todd, safety Taylor Davis and defensive tackle Blake Herold.
Defensive end Leroy Harris III recorded a career-high four tackles for loss against Long Island after leading Kansas with 4.5 sacks in 2025.
Michigan State transfer David Santiago recorded four tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery against Long Island.
Linebacker Trey Lathan returned after leading Kansas with 86 tackles in 2025; he entered 2026 with 198 career tackles and 17 tackles for loss.
Kansas added experienced safeties Corey Gordon and Jaden Harris; Gordon started 12 games for Louisville in 2025, while Harris previously started 13 games for Miami in 2024.
Returning cornerbacks Jalen Todd and Austin Alexander combined for 22 starts for Kansas in 2025.

coaching_changes.fact: Andy Kotelnicki returned to Kansas as associate head coach for 2026 after spending two seasons at Penn State.
Kansas lists Jim Zebrowski as passing game coordinator and quarterbacks coach, Matt Lubick as co-offensive coordinator and tight ends coach, and D.K. McDonald as defensive coordinator.

injury_availability.fact: Wide receiver Cam Pickett, who tied for the team lead with 45 receptions in 2025, did not play in Kansas' 2026 season opener.

offensive_context.fact: Kansas scored five rushing touchdowns against Long Island, with four different players recording a rushing score.
Kansas generated six plays of more than 20 yards and three plays of more than 40 yards against Long Island.
Kansas had averaged 19.7 yards per completion over the previous two seasons, the highest figure in the Big 12 over that span.
Kansas had allowed 45 sacks since the start of the 2023 season, the second-fewest in the Big 12 over that span.

defensive_context.fact: Kansas limited Long Island to 1.1 yards per rushing attempt, allowing 35 yards on 33 carries.
Kansas allowed 26.8 points and 387.2 total yards per game in 2025.
Kansas allowed 214.1 passing yards per game in 2025, its lowest season average since 2001.
Kansas averaged 6.3 tackles for loss per game in 2025, ranking fourth in the Big 12.

special_teams.fact: Kansas added kicker Martin Connington from Michigan State, long snapper Rino Monteforte from California and freshman punter Matt Gill for 2026.
Connington made a 32-yard field goal and all six extra-point attempts against Long Island.
The Game 2 depth chart listed Tate Nagy as the primary punt returner and Dylan Edwards as the primary kickoff returner.

other_relevant.fact: Kansas entered 2026 with eight returning starters—three on offense and five on defense—while losing 15 starters from the 2025 team.
Kansas added 32 transfers for 2026: 13 on offense, 17 on defense and two on special teams.
